title: Best Equipment Finance Software in 2026
summary: Seven equipment finance software platforms compared for lenders and lessors: quoting, credit decisions, underwriting, servicing and AI, and who each one fits.
body_markdown:
Quick answer


Kita is the best equipment finance software in 2026 because it is the one platform that does the whole job: it quotes and structures the deal, collects and fraud-checks the applicant’s documents, checks the invoice, VIN, vendor and lien, spreads the financials through fixed-charge coverage, applies your credit policy as rules-based decisioning, drafts a cited memo and services the contract through billing and collections, on every loan type. Other tools cover part of the deal: Odessa, Abrigo IFSLeaseWorks, Lendscape and Northteq Aurora run the contract, while Aloan, built for bank commercial desks, and Kaaj, focused on broker packages, analyze the credit file. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita is the only one of the seven that covers every job in the scorecard, from quoting and intake to decisioning, the cited memo and servicing. The others split into two groups. Odessa, Abrigo, Lendscape and Northteq run the contract: quotes, booking, billing and servicing. Aloan, built for bank commercial desks, and Kaaj, focused on broker packages, underwrite the file: they read the documents, spread the financials and draft the credit memo.


None of the four contract platforms says on the pages we checked that it drafts a credit memo. Kita, Aloan and Kaaj all do. Kita also applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning, with the credit team keeping final sign-off.


None of the seven posts a list price. Aloan and Kaaj describe how they price, by document volume and by workflow and volume, so ask each for a quote at your own deal count.


**Best overall:** Kita, which quotes the deal, collects the documents from the applicant, checks them, the vendor and the equipment (invoice, VIN and lien), builds the spread through fixed-charge coverage, applies your credit policy, drafts a cited memo and services the contract, all in one platform.


Suppose a contractor applies to finance an excavator. The dealer sends an invoice, and the contractor sends an application, a few months of bank statements and a tax return. Before the lender pays for the machine, it has to answer two questions. Can this business make the payment every month? And if it cannot, what is the machine worth to someone else?


That is equipment finance. In a loan, the borrower owns the equipment from the start and the lender holds a claim on it. In a lease, the lessor owns it, and the business can return, renew or buy it at the end.\[1\] Software for the lender or lessor has to handle the quote, the credit file, the decision, and then years of billing and collections.


Most products that rank for this search describe only part of that. Some run the contract from quote to end of term. Others work on the credit file before the deal is booked. Kita covers both, end to end.


### One equipment deal, five stages


Most products called equipment finance software cover some of these stages. Kita covers all five.

## Equipment finance software for three kinds of lender


The Equipment Leasing and Finance Association (ELFA) tracks new business volume among its member companies. In June 2026 that was $10.5 billion, seasonally adjusted, up 17.2% from a year earlier. Banks accounted for $4.6 billion, captives for $2.9 billion and independents for $2.1 billion.\[5\]


Those three groups buy different software. A bank commercial desk finances equipment inside a wider commercial book. A captive is the finance arm of an equipment maker. An independent lender, often funding deals that vendors and brokers bring in, is built around the equipment. The vendors below say which of the three they are written for, so start there.


## Equipment finance software compared


The scorecard lines up the seven platforms on eight jobs in an equipment deal. Kita is the only platform with a check in every column. A cross means the vendor’s pages do not say it, which does not prove the product cannot do it. Ask the vendor. For Aloan and Kaaj, a cross under the decision engine reflects their design: each says the lender’s underwriter decides.

01


## Kita


Best overall: one platform for the whole equipment deal, from quote and application to cited memo, decision and servicing


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform, and the one product in this guide that covers every stage of an equipment loan or lease. It quotes and structures the deal, takes the application from the applicant, dealer or broker, checks the documents and the equipment, spreads the borrower’s financials, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a credit memo with every figure cited to the document line it came from. After funding it carries the contract through servicing, billing and collections. The lender’s credit team keeps final sign-off.


-


**Quoting, intake and partner portals.** Kita prices and structures loans and leases, including the payment and amortization schedule, and takes applications and full broker, dealer and borrower packages from borrowers, vendors and brokers. It handles every structure: equipment finance agreements, $1 buyout leases, TRAC leases, FMV leases and sale-leasebacks. The AI Credit Officer messages the applicant by SMS, email and the borrower portal, asks for the exact documents the deal needs, checks each upload as it lands and follows up until the file is complete.


-


**Kita Capture: the documents, the equipment and the vendor.** Reads applications, bank statements, tax returns, financial statements, quotes, notes and equipment invoices in any format, flags tampering and forgery patterns, and catches contradictions across the file, such as revenue on the application that the bank statements do not support. It checks the equipment itself: every invoice line is extracted and classified as a hard or soft cost, VINs and serial numbers are decoded, USDOT status and fleet details are pulled for trucking and construction borrowers, and the equipment description is matched across the quote, invoice, note and UCC-1 lien filing. The vendor gets the same checks as the borrower: Secretary of State status, time in business, registered agent, address and web presence.


-


**AI Underwriter and decisioning.** Builds a normalized period-over-period spread, walks EBITDA to EBITDAR and fixed-charge coverage, treats Section 179, bonus depreciation and lease classification the same way every time, and computes debt service coverage with the proposed payment and an editable debt schedule, margin and trend in one pass. Bank statement analysis separates revenue from other deposits and surfaces merchant cash advance stacking, and the borrower’s reported debt schedule is reconciled against the interest expense on the tax return, cited to source. It reads what the spread alone does not show, such as customer concentration or margins falling period after period. It applies the credit policy set for each product as rules-based decisioning, auto-approving, declining or referring each deal per that policy, and drafts the memo in the lender’s own template with every figure cited. The lender’s credit team keeps final sign-off.


-


**Servicing, billing and collections.** Once the deal is booked, Kita runs servicing, billing and collections, and handles end-of-term options, so the same platform that underwrote the contract carries it to the end.


-


**Your stack or Kita’s.** Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system: any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, credit engine or custom workflow. Or it runs the whole process in Intelligent LOS. It works on every loan type, on equipment books and mixed ones: Kita is in production on working capital, SBA 7(a) and 504, commercial real estate and other loan types. Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.


Best for:


Banks, captives, independents and vendor finance teams that want one system to quote, collect, check, spread, decide, draft the memo and service the contract against their own policy, on an equipment book or a mixed one.


02


## Odessa


Best for banks, captives and independents that want one system for the whole lease and loan lifecycle


Odessa describes its software as “your intelligent asset finance software” for equipment and auto finance, built on an AI-enabled platform. Its site lists originations, servicing and remarketing as separate parts of the platform and names three kinds of customer: banks, captives and independents.\[7\]


-


**Originations.** Its originations page lists opportunity management, credit adjudication, pricing and structuring, and interim funding. The modules cover the application, a credit process, a credit decision that uses a rules-based scorecard with automated or manual decision tools, and a deal review with summaries before the contract starts.\[8\]


-


**Platform.** Odessa advertises an API-first architecture, a low-code development toolkit and built-in AI that, in its words, predicts, automates and guides decisions. It also lists remarketing, for equipment that comes back at the end of a contract.\[7\]


-


**What the pages do not describe.** The pages we checked do not describe spreading a borrower’s tax returns and bank statements, checking an equipment invoice or a lien filing, or drafting a credit memo from them. No price is published.\[7,8\]


Best for:


Banks, captives and independents that are replacing or consolidating their system of record and want quoting, credit decisioning, servicing and remarketing in one platform.


03


## Abrigo IFSLeaseWorks


Best for banks, credit unions and independent lessors that want origination and servicing in one cloud system


Abrigo sells IFSLeaseWorks as equipment finance software for banks, credit unions and independent lessors. Abrigo says it digitizes origination, servicing and portfolio management, so a lender can run vendor and broker programs and an in-house portfolio from the same platform.\[9\]


-


**Origination.** Abrigo lists a digital lease application, workflow automation, and tools that let origination partners and internal sales reps price transactions, create amortization schedules, produce quotes, upload documents and track status.\[9\]


-


**Servicing and portfolio.** A customer service portal takes online payments by card or ACH and handles buyout quotes. Abrigo also lists automated renewals and end-of-term management, business intelligence and reporting, and investor and funding tools.\[9\]


-


**Fit.** The platform is hosted on Amazon Web Services and connects to core platforms, CRM systems and document management tools through APIs. Abrigo quotes the technology lead at Navitas Credit Corp on the implementation.\[9\]


-


**What the page does not describe.** The page does not describe spreading a borrower’s financial statements, checking the equipment against an invoice or lien filing, or drafting a credit memo. No price is published.\[9\]


Best for:


Banks, credit unions and independent lessors that run vendor or broker programs and want quoting, servicing and investor reporting on one platform.


04


## Lendscape


Best for lenders that originate elsewhere and want a servicing system built around the asset


Lendscape describes its software as equipment finance software “built around the asset, not the paperwork”: a servicing platform that keeps contracts, collateral and customers in sync. It is the one platform in this guide that says plainly what it leaves out. Pricing and structuring the deal, it says, “happens earlier, in a separate system.”\[10\]


-


**After the deal is booked.** Lendscape manages contract administration, asset tracking, billing, collections and end-of-term processing. It says it services equipment loans, conditional sale agreements and leases in one system.\[10\]


-


**Beside your other systems.** Lendscape says it connects to whatever origination, CRM or general ledger system a lender already runs, and describes itself as 100% API-first.\[10\]


-


**Security and customers.** The page lists ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2 and FSQS certifications, and shows Allica Bank, Compass Business Finance, Liberty Finance and Simply Finance among its clients.\[10\]


-


**What it leaves out.** Lendscape is not an origination or underwriting tool, and the page says so. No price is published.\[10\]


Best for:


Banks, captives and independents that already have an origination process and want to replace servicing, billing and collections with a system that tracks the asset.


05


## Northteq Aurora


Best for independent lenders that already run on Salesforce and want origination and partner portals on top


Northteq’s Aurora is a set of Salesforce apps for the equipment finance industry. The Northteq site says it is trusted by more than 150 lenders and describes Aurora as a way to simplify how lenders originate leases and loans.\[11,12\]


-


**Intake, quotes and documents.** Aurora takes credit applications from any device, structures simple or complex quotes, and lets partners generate their own documents and upload supporting ones. Northteq advertises going from application to documents in three minutes on install.\[11,12\]


-


**Partner portal.** A partner portal gives vendors, brokers and customers real-time visibility into each stage of a deal, with control over what the lender shares with them.\[12\]


-


**Decisioning and integrations.** Northteq’s site names auto decisioning and a credit analytics agent that is part of its Aurora agent suite, and lists integrations with Salesforce, nCino, Aspire and LeaseWave.\[11,12\]


-


**What the pages do not describe.** The pages we checked do not say what the credit analytics agent reads or produces, and do not describe a credit memo. No price is published.\[11,12\]


Best for:


Independent equipment lenders and vendor finance teams that already use Salesforce and want quoting, intake and a partner portal inside it.


06


## Aloan


Best for bank and credit union commercial desks that want cited equipment analysis beside their current LOS


Aloan describes itself as the AI-native commercial loan origination system (LOS) for community banks and credit unions. For equipment loans, its page promises underwriting software that spreads fixed-charge coverage, ties the collateral to the lien filing and reconciles existing debt. It runs as the lender’s LOS or alongside the one the lender already has.\[13,14\]


-


**Spreading.** Aloan spreads a clean EBITDA, walks it to EBITDAR by adding back rent and operating lease payments, then rolls in existing and proposed interest and amortization. It says it treats Section 179, bonus depreciation and vehicle lease classification the same way every time.\[13\]


-


**Collateral and debt.** It matches the equipment description across the quote, invoice, note and the UCC-1 lien filing so the underwriter can confirm they agree before closing. It sets the borrower’s reported debt schedule beside the interest expense on the tax return, both cited to source, and flags unexplained gaps.\[13\]


-


**Structures and memo.** Aloan lists equipment finance agreements, $1 buyout leases, TRAC leases, FMV leases and sale-leasebacks. It assembles the spread, the collateral package and the debt schedule into one place, so the underwriter writes the judgment rather than re-keying the facts.\[13\]


-


**What it leaves out, and what it costs.** Aloan says it does not produce closing documents, book or fund the loan to the core, or make the credit decision. It reports that most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks. It does not post a price: it describes a monthly minimum sized to document volume, a per-document overage rate and a one-time implementation fee, with a quote in one business day.\[14,15\]


Best for:


Community and regional banks and credit unions whose commercial desk finances equipment, and that will keep structure, pricing, closing and booking in other systems.


07


## Kaaj


Best for independent equipment lenders and brokers that want broker packages analyzed beside their LOS


Kaaj calls itself the underwriting OS for equipment finance. It says its AI agents turn broker, dealer and borrower packages into decision-ready credit analysis in minutes, for independent equipment finance companies, small-ticket lenders, vendor and dealer finance teams and broker-driven origination.\[16,17\]


-


**The invoice and the asset.** Kaaj says every line on the invoice is extracted and classified as a hard cost, the equipment itself, or a soft cost such as taxes, delivery, installation and fees. VINs and serial numbers are decoded, and for trucking and construction borrowers a SAFER report adds USDOT status and fleet details.\[16\]


-


**The borrower and the vendor.** The vendor gets the same checks as the borrower: Secretary of State status, time in business, registered agent, address and web presence. Bank statement analysis separates revenue from other deposits and surfaces merchant cash advance stacking, and DSCR is calculated with the proposed payment and an editable debt schedule.\[16\]


-


**Memo and decision.** Kaaj drafts the credit memo in the lender’s own template. It says the lender’s underwriters and credit committee approve, decline or counter, and that Kaaj is the intelligence layer before and around the LOS, with the system of record staying with the lender. It lists integrations with LeasePath, LTi Aspire, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics and Solifi, plus a REST API.\[16\]


-


**Fit and price.** The solutions page names Amur, Smarter Finance USA, Quality Equipment Finance, I90 Financial and Fortis Equipment Funding among its customers. Kaaj does not post a price. It says pricing scales with lending volume, not seat count, and is based on workflow, application volume, products used and integration needs.\[16,18\]


Best for:


Independent lenders, vendor finance teams and brokers that originate small-ticket equipment deals from broker packages and want invoice, vendor and bank statement checks beside their current LOS.


## How to choose equipment finance software


Six questions separate these products more than any feature list.


-


**Which job do you need done?** Quoting, booking and servicing are one job. Reading the file and judging the credit is another. Kita does both in one platform. Odessa, Abrigo, Lendscape and Northteq describe the first, and Aloan and Kaaj the second.\[1,8,9,10,12,13,16\] Lendscape says outright that pricing and structuring happen in a separate system.\[10\]


-


**What kind of lender are you?** ELFA reports banks, captives and independents separately because they run different books.\[5\] Kita works for banks, captives and independents alike, on equipment-only or mixed books. Aloan is written for bank commercial desks, Northteq for independents on Salesforce, and Kaaj for independents, vendor finance teams and brokers. Odessa names all three.\[1,13,11,16,7\]


-


**Does it read the file, or only hold it?** A system that stores the application and the documents is not the same as one that spreads the financials and writes the analysis. Ask to see a DSCR built from your own applicant’s bank statements, and who has to key in the numbers.


-


**Can you trace every figure?** Every figure in Kita’s memo, from the spread to the debt reconciliation and the lien match, links to the document line it came from. Aloan says its debt reconciliation is cited to source.\[1,13\] Ask to click from a coverage ratio to the page it came from, and whether an analyst’s override is recorded.


-


**Does it enforce your policy, or a generic one?** Each lender sets its own minimum time in business, deal size and coverage. Kita applies the credit policy you set for each product as rules-based decisioning, approving, declining or referring each deal, and Odessa lists a rules-based scorecard.\[1,8\] Give each vendor your policy and see what it flags.


-


**Does it replace your LOS or run beside it, and what will it cost?** Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, and can also run as the LOS. Aloan and Kaaj say they work alongside the LOS you have, and Lendscape connects to the origination system you run.\[2,14,16,10\] None posts a list price, so ask for a quote at your deal volume, then run three closed equipment files through each shortlisted tool and compare the result with your analysts’ work.


Our recommendation is Kita: it is the one platform that answers yes to all six questions and covers quoting, underwriting, decisioning and servicing, so a lender does not have to pair two systems. If you only need part of the job, Odessa, Abrigo and Northteq run quoting, booking and servicing, Lendscape covers servicing, Aloan analyzes the credit file for bank commercial desks, and Kaaj analyzes broker packages.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best equipment finance software?


Kita is the best equipment finance software for most lenders and lessors because it covers the whole deal in one platform: quoting and structuring, application intake, document, vendor and equipment checks (invoice, VIN and lien), spreading through fixed-charge coverage, rules-based decisioning against your credit policy, a cited credit memo, and servicing, billing and collections. Other tools cover part of the deal: Odessa, Abrigo IFSLeaseWorks, Lendscape and Northteq Aurora run the contract, Aloan analyzes the credit file for bank commercial desks, and Kaaj analyzes broker packages. Run one of your closed equipment files through Kita to see the result.


### What is equipment finance software?


It is software that lenders and lessors use to run equipment loans and leases. Some products quote deals, take applications and score them, some book, bill and collect for the life of the contract, and some, called underwriting software, read the borrower’s documents, work out whether the business can make the payment and draft the credit memo.


### What is the difference between equipment leasing software and equipment finance underwriting software?


Equipment leasing software manages the contract: pricing, booking, billing, collections and the end of the lease. Equipment finance underwriting software works on the credit file before the deal is booked: it reads the application, bank statements and financials, tests the deal against the lender’s policy and drafts the memo. Kita does both in one platform, so a lender does not have to connect two systems.


### What is the best AI software for equipment finance underwriting?


Kita is the best AI software for equipment finance underwriting, on every equipment structure and every loan type. It collects the documents from the applicant, checks them for fraud, classifies every invoice line, decodes VINs and serial numbers, checks the vendor and matches the equipment to the lien filing, builds the spread through fixed-charge coverage, reconciles the debt schedule, surfaces merchant cash advance stacking, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a memo in the lender’s template with every figure cited. Aloan and Kaaj also work on the equipment credit file in narrower roles: Aloan adds fixed-charge coverage and lien filing checks for bank commercial desks, and Kaaj checks invoices, VINs and vendors for broker packages.


### Do we have to replace our loan origination or servicing system to add AI underwriting?


No. Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, credit engine or custom workflow, and lenders that want one system from quote to servicing can run the whole process in Kita’s Intelligent LOS. Aloan and Kaaj each say they work alongside an existing LOS, and servicing systems such as Lendscape connect to whatever origination system a lender runs.


### What is Kita and how does it underwrite equipment finance deals?


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform. On an equipment deal it quotes and structures the loan or lease, its AI Credit Officer collects the documents from the applicant, Kita Capture reads and fraud-checks them along with the invoice, VIN and lien filing, and the AI Underwriter builds the spread, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a memo with every figure cited to its source. Kita then services the contract. The lender’s credit team keeps final sign-off.
